purpose: Select discriminating evidence for the interface-support handoff. The catalog offers five candidate local supports (G000–G004) all under parent R15_V3_COMPATIBLE, all with the same observable contract (predictive_bridge_to_learning_end vs actual_ancestor_at_learning_end), same clock_policy fixed, same operator pointwise, and identical numerical options except for the atom_slots/pocket_sites/orientation_triplets defining each region. Because the numerical program is held constant across groups, the only discriminating axis is the local support identity. I need real tool evidence to (a) confirm which of these regions actually has ancestral support in the real lineage (ancestor), (b) check whether any of these regions shows selection enrichment rather than drift (selection_trend), and (c) check whether the parent controller already responded to these regions (controller_response) and whether any of them belongs to a known failure family (failure_history). I will not invent results; if a tool returns no support for a region, that region is dropped rather than guessed. Two requests are issued to cover the most informative pair: the widest support (G000, 3 slots with orientation triplets) versus the narrowest (G001, 2 slots, no orientation triplets), since the prior campaign readout warns that support background matters and that a 3-point region did not replicate the wider-support benefit. This pair is the minimal contrast that can distinguish 'support size/background drives the effect' from 'any local support works' before the handoff.
